title: Tend: Local Dashboard for All Claude Code Sessions Launches
summary: Tend launches as an open-source local dashboard that aggregates all Claude Code sessions in one interface, eliminating tab sprawl for developers.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Tend launches as an open-source local dashboard that consolidates all Claude Code sessions into one unified interface for developers.
- The tool addresses tab management challenges by providing a centralized view of multiple coding projects without switching browser contexts.
- Available immediately on GitHub, Tend runs locally and integrates with existing Claude Code workflows for streamlined development.


Developers working with multiple Claude Code sessions now have a centralized solution. Tend, an open-source local dashboard, officially launched on November 22, 2026, providing a single interface to manage all Claude Code interactions without the browser tab chaos that typically accompanies multi-project development workflows.


## What Tend Does


Tend consolidates every Claude Code session into one local page, eliminating the need to juggle multiple browser tabs or windows. The tool runs locally on a developer's machine, aggregating active and historical sessions from Anthropic's AI coding assistant into a unified dashboard. Developers can view, switch between, and organize their Claude Code projects from a single access point.


The open-source nature of Tend means developers can inspect the codebase, contribute improvements, or modify the tool to fit specific workflow requirements. The project is hosted on GitHub under the repository Geekgineer/tend, making it accessible to the broader development community.


## Solving the Tab Management Problem


As Claude Code adoption has grown throughout 2026, developers have reported workflow friction from managing multiple concurrent coding sessions. Each new project or context switch typically requires opening another browser tab, leading to cluttered workspaces and lost session context. Tend addresses this pain point by creating a persistent local interface that tracks all sessions regardless of browser state.


The dashboard approach also provides better session history visibility. Developers can review past interactions, revisit previous coding contexts, and maintain continuity across work sessions without searching through browser history or bookmarks.


## Release Date and Availability


Tend officially released on November 22, 2026, and is immediately available through its GitHub repository. The tool requires local installation and integrates with existing Claude Code workflows without requiring changes to how developers interact with Anthropic's platform. Installation instructions and documentation are provided in the repository README.


## Technical Architecture


According to the repository details, Tend operates as a local server that interfaces with Claude Code sessions. The architecture prioritizes privacy by keeping all session data on the developer's machine rather than transmitting information to external services. This local-first approach aligns with security-conscious development practices, particularly for teams working with proprietary codebases.


Key features highlighted in the initial release include:


- Real-time session aggregation across multiple Claude Code instances
- Persistent session history with searchable archives
- Lightweight local server footprint
- Cross-platform compatibility for major operating systems


## What This Means


Tend represents the growing ecosystem of third-party tools built around AI coding assistants like Claude Code. As these platforms mature, developers are creating specialized utilities to optimize workflows and address friction points in daily usage. The open-source model ensures the tool can evolve with community input, potentially establishing session management patterns that benefit the broader AI-assisted development landscape. For teams scaling their use of Claude Code across multiple projects, Tend offers an immediate productivity improvement by centralizing what was previously scattered across dozens of browser tabs.
